name: AI Viewing Scheduler and Booking Confirmation

options.systemMessage:
You are a professional real estate assistant. Draft a warm personalized email proposing three viewing slots for a property to a prospective buyer.

The email should:
- Feel personally written by the agent — not automated
- Reference the lead name and property naturally
- Present three viewing options clearly and invitingly
- Encourage booking via the Calendly link provided
- Be professional but conversational
- Body maximum 3-4 sentences
- Never mention AI or automation

Format email_body as two parts separated by \n\n:
  Part 1: Greeting line only e.g. "Hi Sarah,"
  Part 2: Message body as one paragraph

Output ONLY valid JSON, no preamble, no markdown:
{
  "email_subject": "short friendly subject line",
  "email_body": "Hi {name},\n\nBody here.",
  "sms_message": "SMS under 160 chars — friendly reminder version"
}

parameters.content:
## AI Viewing Scheduler and Booking Confirmation

Automates the entire property viewing journey, from the initial request through booking confirmation and 24-hour reminders, without any manual coordination.

### How it works
**Phase 1:** A viewing request arrives via webhook. AI drafts a personalized proposal email with three available slots and a Calendly booking link. The lead receives it within seconds. Choose your preferred AI engine — Gemini, ChatGPT, or Claude — in the Configuration node.

**Phase 2:** When the lead books via Calendly, a confirmation email sends to both lead and agent, a Google Calendar event is created with both attendees, and the viewing status updates in Google Sheets. Exactly 24 hours before the viewing, reminder emails send to both lead and agent.

### Requirements
- **Gmail** OAuth2 — all emails
- **Gemini** API key — if using Gemini (default)
- **OpenAI** API key — if using ChatGPT
- **Anthropic** API key — if using Claude (in Config node)
- **Google Calendar** OAuth2 — event creation
- **Google Sheets** OAuth2 — viewing log
- **Calendly** — free account + webhook setup

### Setup
1. Connect **Gmail**, **Google Calendar**, and **Google Sheets** credentials.
2. Connect your chosen AI credential.
3. Update both **Configuration nodes** — Phase 1 and Phase 2 each have their own.
4. Set your availability hours in the Configuration node — empty = unavailable that day.
5. Register the Phase 2 webhook URL in Calendly → Integrations → Webhooks → invitee.created.

### Customization
- Change AI_ENGINE to Gemini, ChatGPT, or Claude.
- Adjust SLOT_DAYS_AHEAD and VIEWING_DURATION.
- Edit availability hours per day in Config node.
- Chain from **Templates #5**, **#6**, or **#10** by sending an HTTP Request to the Phase 1 webhook URL.

### Template#5
https://n8n.io/workflows/17258-qualify-facebook-lead-ads-and-send-follow-ups-with-gemini-gmail-and-sheets/

### Template#6
https://n8n.io/workflows/17409-qualify-inbound-real-estate-leads-from-gmail-with-gemini-and-hubspot/

### Template#10
https://n8n.io/workflows/18329-match-new-property-listings-to-buyer-leads-with-gemini-gmail-and-sheets/

## Phase 1 — Viewing Request Entry
Webhook is the default. It accepts a POST from any website form, CRM, or previous QualMatic template. Google Sheet trigger is optional and disabled. Both produce identical output into the Normalize node.

## Request Normalization & Slot Generation
Incoming request is normalized from webhook or Google Sheet format into clean named fields. All agent settings — availability hours, AI engine, Calendly slug, and property details — are configured in the Agent Configuration node. Three viewing slots are calculated automatically from the availability windows. Empty hours = that day unavailable.

## Choose Your AI Engine
Switch node routes to Gemini, ChatGPT, or Claude based on AI_ENGINE in the Configuration node. Only one fires per execution and the others are skipped. All three produce identical JSON output read by the same Parse AI Output node. Add credentials for whichever engine you prefer. All three can be connected simultaneously.

## Viewing Proposal — Phase 1 Output
Lead receives a personalized email with three available viewing slots and a Calendly booking link. Slots are calculated from the availability windows in the Configuration node — no manual diary checking. Every request logs to Google Sheets with Status = Pending.

## Phase 2 — Booking Confirmation & Reminder

Fires independently when the lead books via Calendly. No connection to Phase 1 — shares only Google Sheets. Phase 2 has its own Configuration node — update both when changing agent details.

## Phase 2 Configuration & Booking Details
Phase 2 runs as a separate execution and cannot 
access Phase 1 nodes. Update agent details in 
this Configuration node independently.
Booking details — lead name, email, viewing time, 
cancel and reschedule links — are extracted from 
the Calendly webhook payload here.

## 24-Hour Reminder
The Wait node pauses execution until exactly 24 hours before the viewing start time — then fires reminder emails to both lead and agent simultaneously. Cancel and reschedule links are included in both reminder emails.

## Confirmation & Calendar Event
When Calendly fires the booking webhook, a Google Calendar event is created with both lead and agent as attendees — both receive a calendar invite. Confirmation emails send to lead and agent in parallel. Google Sheets updates Status from Pending to Booked.

## Update Phase 1 Configuration
Set these values:
AGENT_NAME, AGENT_EMAIL, AGENT_PHONE
CALENDAR_ID CALENDLY_USERNAME and CALENDLY_EVENT_SLUG
PROPERTY_ADDRESS and PROPERTY_URL
AI_ENGINE — Gemini / ChatGPT / Claude
Availability hours — empty string means unavailable.

## Update Phase 2 Configuration
Phase 2 runs as a separate execution and cannot 
read Phase 1's Configuration node.
Update AGENT_NAME, AGENT_EMAIL, AGENT_PHONE, 
CALENDAR_ID, and PROPERTY_ADDRESS here too for keeping both Config nodes in sync.

## Register This URL in Calendly
Copy this webhook's Production URL and paste it into Calendly → Integrations → Webhooks.
Event to subscribe: invitee.created
Requires a permanent public n8n URL — not localhost. For local testing use the Test URL with a tunnel.
